To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the MRSA strains isolated in pigs were susceptible to the disinfectant glutaraldehyde at a concentration of 0.5%, and that they presented phenotypic resistences to the antibiotics penicillin, ampicillin, cefoxitin and gentamicin.
all MRSA strains isolated from healthy pigs were susceptible to antiseptics, disinfectants and a broad range of antibiotics.
the strains of methicillins‐resistant Stapylococcus aureus, which were studied in this research, showed a great susceptibility to disinfectants.

an emerging problem, and the results obtained may be used as an alert for future studies.
the phenotypic characterization of strains of MRSA isolated from pigs.
the study of the phenotypic resistance of strains of MRSA isolated from healthy pigs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of the recommended concentrations of the disinfectants and antiseptics used in our research, would be effective in the treatment of MRSA infections, and that their use in the prevention of these infections would be advisable.

the disinfectants and antiseptics used in the present study, as well as other similar products, could be useful for the prevention of MRSA infections in pigs, and that the use of antibiotics for the treatment of MRSA infections should be limited.
the use of disinfectants and antiseptics in the prevention of infections by MRSA in pigs is highly recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of antiseptices and disinfectants is an effective alternative for the treatment of MRSA infections.
the use of antiseptical and disinfectant agents, such as those tested in this research, would be a more effective alternative to the use of antibiotics in the treatment of MRSA‐related infections.

the strains of MRSA isolated from pigs in this research are phenotypically resistant to antibiotics, but susceptible to antiseptics, disinfectants and silver nitrate, which may be a useful alternative for the treatment of MRSA infections in pigs and in other animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phenotypic resistance of MRSA strains to antibiotics is not necessarily accompanied by resistance to the disinfectant agents used.
the use of antiseptico‐disinfectants in the treatment and prevention against MRSA infection is a viable alternative to the use of antibiotics.
the strains of MRSA that we studied were not resistant to the disinfecting agents used in the swine industry.
